_comment: max_states_per_point stays at 200. The cap was considered and priced, not
missed. One test function exceeds it: 'a setter that cannot copy changes
nothing and sets the failure tag' at src/capi/node_properties.zig:8598. The
test drives about forty exports through one allocator that refuses, so each
call forks the state space and the entry node of the test reaches the
ceiling. zwanzig then reports three analysis-limit-exceeded lines for it and
no dataflow finding for that function.
The number that would clear it is known. Measured with 'zwanzig --config
.zwanzig.json --max-states-per-point N --threads 8'. Over src/capi as a
directory: N=200 wall 1.3 s and 66 MB, N=400 1.7 s and 84 MB, N=800 3.4 s and
118 MB, all reporting the finding. Over src/capi/node_properties.zig alone:
reporting it, and N=3200 34.2 s and N=4096 32.6 s, neither reporting it. So
the clearing boundary is between 2800 and 3200 and the smallest power of two
above it is 4096.
The budget stays at 200 because the price is wrong. Over the gate file list
of 126 files, N=200 runs the stage in 3.5 s and reports 65 findings, and
N=4096 runs it in 30.0 s and reports 62. The 3 findings that leave are
exactly the analysis-limit-exceeded lines for that one test, so the 8.6x
cost buys the analysis budget of a single test and surfaces no new defect.
The 3 lines are accepted at 200 rather than bought. Raising the budget to
close them costs about 27 seconds on every gate run for the internal state
space of one test, which is a bad trade.
